_comment: The capability DAG, as data. docs/capability-dag.md is prose about it;
THIS is what tools/compile_dag.py reads and what README.md renders from.
A node is not green because someone wrote that it is. Every node names the
evidence that would make it green, and the compiler checks that evidence.
This document twice carried findings that had already been fixed -- the
modal_dp exc hazard, and red on four repaired drum circuits -- because a
human maintained it by hand. Compiling it from evidence is the fix.
class: 'implementation' = tested against OUR model. 'fidelity' = tested
against an EXTERNAL reference. A subsystem with no fidelity evidence is
UNVALIDATED however many implementation tests pass -- see issue #45.

covers: files whose change invalidates this node's evidence -> STALE. slow: too slow for a push; status is read from docs/dag-results.json, which the nightly job writes. GREEN means the evidence RAN AND PASSED at a commit, never merely that a file exists.

covers must name EVERY input whose change invalidates the node. S1 and S3 once listed only synth_top.v, so they stayed GREEN through voice RTL and ROM changes -- compiling a status document does not fix an incomplete definition of what the evidence depends on.

M3.name: Matches software references
M3.note: the committed comparison RESULT, not the estimator unit tests -- those consume no reference audio and cannot show we compared anything. REFUSED on purpose and correctly: this file is a dict of 49 per-case measurement ARRAYS with no top-level verdict key, so compile_dag has nothing to read. It is left unjudged rather than given an evidence_requires, because the only candidate substring is already defeated by the committed file -- it contains '"ok": true' 133 times AND '"ok": false' 8 times, so a substring guard would PASS a file carrying 8 failing comparisons (rule 8). Clearing this needs a re-run of the reference comparison that emits a top-level verdict over all 49 cases; until then the minimoog UNVALIDATED warning this restores is the true state (#45, #791).

M4.name: Matches real hardware
M4.blocked: 0 of 222 Legowelt recordings qualify -- needs one documented self-oscillation clip

M5.name: Noise, osc-3 modulation, full waveform set

S1.name: Routed on gf180, DRC clean
S1.note: the verdict is DERIVED by pnr/orfs/make_verdict.py from the run's own stage metrics, not read from 6_report.json: that file declares no verdict AND carries no DRC count of any kind (grep -ic drc returns 0), so the 'DRC clean' in this node's name lives in 5_2_route.json. Regenerate with `python pnr/orfs/make_verdict.py pnr/orfs/evidence/synth_top/joined-d1e5068`; `--check` and pnr/orfs/test_make_verdict.py fail on a hand-edited verdict. max-capacitance violations are 2 and are disclosed-not-gating in the verdict (docs/pnr-synth-top.md s.4.1). No sign-off DRC deck exists on gf180 and no LVS was run.

S2.name: Fits a real shuttle padframe
S2.blocked: LibreLane half-slot, in flight: padcells 0 -> 754 placed with all 5 wafer.space IP macros, 73.07 % core utilisation, drum_regs 3,520/3,520 flops placed on the run's own DEF. Detailed routing has NOT completed (iteration 60 of a 64 cap, 1 Metal2 short), so there is no final router DRC count, no post-route antenna check and no post-route STA at any corner. The verdict this node will read is pnr/shuttle/evidence/halfslot-verdict.json ('passed' = the AREA question only); finish it with pnr/shuttle/finish_halfslot.py finish. docs/pnr-shuttle-halfslot.md, PR #348

S3.name: FPGA build of the real engine
S3.note: 'RESULT: routed.' is emitted by fpga/scripts/pnr_report.py ONLY for its ROUTED verdict, which requires nextpnr exit 0, a populated utilisation block, 'Routing complete.', a Max-frequency line AFTER that marker, every post stage exit 0 and a non-empty bitstream -- and that script refuses to overwrite a committed report on any other verdict (its DOES-NOT-FIT and REFUSED states write 'RESULT: DOES NOT FIT' / 'RESULT: REFUSED' instead). Rule 8, what satisfies this substring while violating its intent: (a) a bare 'PASS at' substring would have been satisfied by the post-placement ESTIMATE line even with a failing post-route line, which is why the substring is the routed verdict and not the Fmax; (b) a HAND-EDITED or STALE committed report -- the substring tests committed text, not the run. The guards against (b) are this node's `covers` list (any RTL change turns it STALE) and fpga/test_pnr_report.py, not the substring. Says nothing about whether the design computes the right samples (rule 3).
